title: LEGO Confirms UCS Millennium Falcon and X-Mansion Are Retiring Soon
summary: LEGO has officially added several big-name sets, including the UCS Millennium Falcon and X-Men X-Mansion, to its 'retiring soon' list, meaning they'll leave shelves by the end of 2026.
bodyMarkdown:

Among the newly added sets are 75192 Millennium Falcon (the UCS Star Wars flagship), 76294 X-Men: The X-Mansion, and 10326 Natural History Museum. This is an official confirmation from LEGO, not a rumour, so if any of these are on your wishlist, now's the time to act before stock disappears for good.

## Why it matters
Retirement announcements are a big deal for collectors and fans alike. Once these sets are gone, they typically become harder to find and prices on the secondary market usually rise. The UCS Millennium Falcon in particular is one of LEGO's most iconic and sought-after Star Wars sets, so its retirement will likely prompt a rush of last-minute purchases.

title: LEGO Ideas: Huge Polar Express Fan Build Hits 10,000 Supporters
summary: A giant fan-made Polar Express model has reached the 10K support threshold on LEGO Ideas, joining eight other projects in the platform's third 2026 review round.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A fan-designed LEGO Ideas project recreating the train from The Polar Express has reached the 10,000-supporter milestone, according to Brick Fanatics. Created by fan designer Olivier312, the model uses 4,930 pieces and measures around 187.5cm long. It includes 12 minifigures (with a caribou and the Ebenezer Scrooge puppet counted in that total), plus play features like removable sections and sliding parts designed to recreate scenes from the film. The designer had hoped to motorise the train but reportedly found it too heavy.

This submission joins eight other projects that have already qualified for LEGO Ideas' third review round of 2026, which is due to close for entries on 4 January 2027. LEGO Ideas review rounds decide which fan-submitted concepts get considered for official production as real sets.

## Why it matters
Reaching 10,000 votes doesn't guarantee a set will be made — LEGO still has to choose it during the review stage. But it's a big deal for fans of large-scale builds and licensed pop culture models, and it shows the kind of ambitious scale fan designers are aiming for lately, following recently revealed large sets like 21373 Downton Abbey.

## What to watch next
The review period runs until January 2027, so it'll be a while before we know if The Polar Express, or any of the other eight qualifying projects, gets the green light to become an official set. Worth noting: this is a **rumour/speculation stage** — nothing is confirmed as an actual product yet, only that it has qualified for review consideration.
